text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA
- We have made an important step towards revitalisation of Yugoslav-Romanian agrarian cooperation, said Yugoslav agriculture minister Nedeljko Sipovac during visit to Bucharest.

- The Yugoslav government's announcement that it will issue its first tranche of Treasury bills on May 12 after a five-year break shows its commitment to obtain necessary funds through open market operations, state news agency Tanjug comments.
- Yugoslavia's monetary credit policy is successful, says deputy governor of the National Bank of Yugoslavia Bozidar Gazivoda.
- Frozen foreign currency savings to be returned to depositors by 2008 at the latest. Federal government to make a decision on the issue by mid-May.
- The opposition is a prisoner of the past, says newly-appointed member of the Socialist Party of Serbia main board Zeljko Simic.
- The 17th anniversary of President Josip Broz Tito's death was marked at the Belgrade memorial centre.
- Registration of Bosnian refugees for elections started in Yugoslavia and will last to June 7.
NASA BORBA
- Any solution for Kosovo must honor human rights, says U.N. Human Rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn during visit to Pristina.
- Assembly of Croatian Serbs in Eastern Slavonia calls for annullment of recently held local elections over irregularities.

- Montenegrin shipping company Jugooceanija has started operating as a shareholders' society. Of its 100 million German mark assets 26 percent go to funds, 26.3 percent to the republic of Montenegro and 47.7 percent to the workers.

- Montenegriin Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic is the most popular politician according to a poll conducted by agency Damar with 37.8 percent of those polled saying they would like to see him as president of the republic.
- Independent teachers' trade union Nezavisnost will stage a warning strike on May 9 if teachers' outstanding salaries are not paid by that date.
- Yugoslav television channel to be opened soon, says Yugoslav Information Minister Goran Matic.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Revenue from agricultural exports planneld to reach one billion dollars in 1997, says Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic.

- Yugoslav metal works Rudarsko Metalurski Kombinat Trepca, Jugobanka bank and export-import firm Genex will sign a $517 million five-year deal with Greek metal trade company Mitlineos in Athens Monday.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Gray economy has assumed serious proportions, says Yugoslav Deputy Prime Minister Vojin Djukanovic.
BORBA

- The Serbian government has taken 20 strategic measurs for development of the agrarian sector, the most important being deferrment of fiscal duty payments to November, says Serbian agriculture minister Jovan Babovic. Agrarian 1997 exports planned to reach one billion dollars.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin public company for marine protection spent over 10 million dinars in 1996 for the protection of beaches, the sea and the coastal area.
- U.N. Special Human Rights rapporteur Elisabeth Rehn visited Montenegrin northern municipality of Plevlja Sunday. -- Belgrade newsroom + 381 11 222 4305
